砂.meaning: A sculptor keeps chipping at a <part>stone</part>, aiming for the perfect statue. Every day there's a <part>few</part> bits less of it: a boulder, a brick, a pebble, a crumb. In the end, all that's left of her masterpiece is a pinch of <kanji>sand</kanji>.
砂.on: She sweeps it into an empty <sound>sa</sound>rdine tin and calls it art.
砂.kun: The tin sits on a beach stall between the <sound>su</sound>shi and the <sound>na</sound>an, and nobody notices it at all.

糖.meaning: In a palace of old <part>china</part>, the cooks boil a pot of <part>rice</part> for a hundred days, stirring until it turns to sticky, sparkling white crystals. The emperor licks one spoonful and grins. They have invented <kanji>sugar</kanji>.
糖.on: He eats so much that a sugar lump rolls off the table and lands on his big <sound>toe</sound>.

活.meaning: On the hottest day of the year, a frog lies flat on a lily pad, too limp to croak, until a few <part>water drops</part> land on its <part>tongue</part>. It blinks, and suddenly it's leaping from pad to pad, singing and splashing everyone. Nothing in the pond is as <kanji>lively</kanji>.
活.on: It celebrates by gulping down a crumbed <sound>katsu</sound> cutlet in one go.
活.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' squeals a dragonfly, as the frog everyone thought was done for springs up: it lives!

育.meaning: A woman finds a baby <part>moon</part> no bigger than a plum and keeps it in a jar with a <part>lid</part>. She rocks it in the crook of her <part>elbow</part>, feeds it starlight, and every month it grows rounder. Year after year she will <kanji>bring up</kanji> the moon.
育.on: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' she squeals, shooing away a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo that tries to lay its egg in the jar.
育.kun: It grows up on the <sound>so</sound>fa, watching her throw <sound>da</sound>rts at the stars.

応.meaning: A lonely <part>heart</part> spots a sign on a garden <part>shed</part>: 'Wanted: someone to keep the hens warm.' It fills in the form, draws itself a smile and slides it under the door. It's the first job it has ever dared to <kanji>apply</kanji> for.
応.on: The interview is held under a huge <sound>oa</sound>k, and the hens ask all the questions.
応.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala answers the shed door with the result: '<sound>Ta</sound>-da! You're hired!'

界.meaning: A beetle lives <part>jammed in</part> between the squares of one <part>rice field</part>, squeezed so tight it can't see past the next stalk. It thinks the paddy is everything there is. To the beetle, this one field is the whole <kanji>world</kanji>.
界.on: One day a <sound>ki</sound>te string snags it and lifts it high, and it sees a million more fields.
